findings.title: Unclosed/malformed each block in group member list
findings.body: The template uses `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` without a corresponding `{{/each}}` and without block syntax (`{{#each ...}}`). In Ember/Handlebars this will either fail template compilation or cause the surrounding markup to be treated incorrectly, breaking the admin group member list.

findings.title: remove_member deletes with an integer ID instead of a user record
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an integer ID to an ActiveRecord association `delete`, which expects User records (and may not behave correctly for a through association). This is likely a no-op or raises an exception, so members may not actually be removed. Use the join association or load the user first, e.g. `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all` or `group.users.find(user_id)` followed by `group.users.delete(user)`.

findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When the member count is exactly divisible by the page limit (for example 50 members with limit 50), this returns one extra page. The UI will show an extra page and allow navigating to an empty member list.

findings.title: findMembers allows offset equal to total user_count
findings.body: `findMembers` clamps offset with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`, which permits `offset == user_count`. That requests a page starting after the last record and returns an empty list. The clamp should prevent moving past the last valid page, or pagination should be computed from page numbers rather than allowing offset equal to total.

findings.title: Public members endpoint does not validate limit/offset
findings.body: The public members endpoint accepts arbitrary `limit` and `offset` values and only calls `.to_i`. Negative values can produce invalid SQL or errors, `limit=0` can cause confusing client behavior, and very large limits can load and serialize all group members. This creates a resource-exhaustion risk on a public endpoint.

findings.title: Group creation ignores submitted alias_level
findings.body: The JavaScript model sends `alias_level` when creating a group, but the `create` action only assigns `name` and `visible`. Any alias level chosen while creating a new group is silently discarded, so the group is created with the default alias level.

findings.title: Members endpoint response shape changed from array to object
findings.body: The members endpoint now returns `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` instead of a serialized array. This changes the public JSON contract and will break existing API clients or integrations that expect the previous array response.

findings.title: add_members silently ignores invalid usernames and whitespace
findings.body: `add_members` splits the comma-separated usernames without stripping whitespace and ignores unknown usernames. A payload like `'a, b'` may fail to match `' b'`, and the action still returns success even if no valid users were added, giving administrators no feedback about failed additions.

findings.title: visible parameter handling only accepts the string 'true'
findings.body: `params[:visible] == "true"` treats JSON boolean `true` as false. If an API client sends a JSON payload with `visible: true`, the group will be saved as not visible. The controller should cast the parameter using a boolean-aware conversion.

findings.title: Save error handler assumes JSON error payload
findings.body: The save failure handler executes `$.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors`. If the request fails with no response body, a non-JSON body, or a different error format, this line throws and masks the original failure instead of showing a useful error message.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group test uses PUT instead of DELETE
findings.body: The spec tests `remove_member` with `xhr :put`, but the route is defined as DELETE. This does not exercise the real HTTP verb/route and can hide routing or method mismatches.

findings.title: No specs cover the changed public members endpoint
findings.body: The public `members` action was changed to add pagination metadata and a new response envelope, but no controller/request specs cover the new payload shape, limit/offset behavior, invalid parameters, or authorization boundaries.
